clue.text: Sway to and fro, leave office about to be unwell

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the office-leaving word goes round the illness word

parts.note: to leave an office or post is to vacate it
unwell means ill

explanation.surface: An official wavers, steps down and is about to fall sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container, and 'to be' is only a link before the illness word.
explanation.definitionFit: To vacillate is to waver, swinging between opinions or physically swaying back and forth.

parts.note: read as the name of the fourth month in the French tongue, not the song title

explanation.surface: The romantic song title about springtime in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase looks like the famous song; read literally it asks for the French word for the month.
explanation.definitionFit: The French language calls the fourth month of the year by this name.

clue.text: Sneering at one boy in charge

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
Ron is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a lad who is in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironic remarks are mocking and sardonic, much like a sneer.

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the run of words sunlit China

explanation.surface: Fruit grown in sun-drenched China.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a variant spelling of lychee, a small sweet Chinese fruit.

indicators.note: in places the engineers abbreviation within the word the

parts.note: taken as written
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Engineers form part of a little team.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers are a British Army corps, a stock crossword source of two letters; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is about as small as a group can be, so the number naming it serves.

parts.note: a woman elected to sit in the US legislature, the House of Representatives

explanation.surface: A woman who speaks on behalf of others.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that 'representative' is meant in the US political sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A US member of the House of Representatives who is a woman is so styled.

parts.note: degrees of temperature: the phrase called out in a hunt game as a seeker nears the hidden thing, here the solution at 19

explanation.surface: Moving step by step toward a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: In the children's game of hunting for a hidden object, players say this phrase as the seeker draws near; 19-across is the solution being sought, and the degrees are of temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means coming closer to the right solution, as in a hide-and-seek guessing game.

clue.text: Furniture seen on more than three hoardings?

definitions.text: Furniture seen on more than three hoardings?

parts.words: Furniture seen on more than three hoardings?
parts.note: hoardings carry posters, and four is more than three: a piece of bedroom furniture with four corner posts

explanation.surface: Wondering about furniture advertised on numerous billboards.
explanation.walkthrough: A hoarding is a British billboard; the bed's four corner posts are punningly treated as four advertising posters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a bed with a tall post at each corner, often hung with curtains.

parts.note: literally, catch the scent of a rodent; idiomatically, sense that something is wrong

explanation.surface: Picking up the scent of a pest with misgiving.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to suspect trickery, literally to sniff out a rodent.

clue.text: Sweets on a bunch of threads found in the garden

parts.note: candy is sweets, especially in American usage
a tuft is a bunch of threads, hairs or grass

explanation.surface: Sweets lying on a clump of threads out in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link; the definition loosely describes a garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Candytuft is a flowering garden plant, Iberis, common in borders and rockeries.

clue.text: Important person to return into the grips of Greek character by third of July

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Important person to return into the grips of Greek character by third of July'. MOGUL needs OG (GO reversed) inside MU plus L, but no clue word gives GO; a word appears to be missing.
annotationWithheld.clue: Important person to return into the grips of Greek character by third of July

parts.note: one performer among a crowd scene with no lines of their own

explanation.surface: A lone performer on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single' suggests one star alone; this actor is a nameless individual in a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A film extra is a non-speaking performer hired to fill out a crowd scene.

parts.note: AC is aircraftman, the lowest RAF rank
rid means freed or liberated

explanation.surface: A pilot is set free, sharply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrid taste or smell is pungent and biting.

clue.text: An attempt by artist at the market-place

parts.note: a go is an attempt
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Someone has a try at painting in the market square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' and 'at the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece the agora was the public square used for trade and assembly.

indicators.note: movement means the letters of chart are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A diagram showing motion of a toothed bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has lost its spaces: read 'Chart movement of a toothed rack'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratch is a ratchet, a bar with teeth engaged by a pawl.

clue.text: Way-out name included of a benevolent person

indicators.note: included means the name abbreviation is placed within the exit word

parts.note: a door is a way out

explanation.surface: A generous person's name is put on an exit.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside DOOR; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor gives money or goods freely, the act of a charitable person.

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the phrase for a whopper is to be taken in a different order

parts.note: a whopper is a big lie

explanation.surface: A tall story told by a German scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: A whopper is a BIG LIE; 'perhaps' lets the two words swap places.
explanation.definitionFit: Justus von Liebig was a nineteenth-century German chemist famed for agricultural chemistry.

definitions.meaning: in cricket, the first pair of batsmen are said to have done this

explanation.surface: Began at the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: To open is to begin; in cricket the batsmen who go in first open the innings.

clue.text: Note a concoction made of cereals

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so the letters of note a are mixed

explanation.surface: A recipe note for a dish made of grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaten means made from oats, a cereal crop.

indicators.note: redesigned means the letters of a Wren's are refashioned into a new shape

parts.note: the possessive s counts as a letter here

explanation.surface: A naval servicewoman's outfit has been restyled.
explanation.walkthrough: A Wren was a member of the Women's Royal Naval Service; 'suit' is a verb, as in 'that will serve'.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet a need or serve a purpose is a sense shared by both words.

clue.text: Surpass in ingenuity without possibly losing aspiration

indicators.note: possibly signals that the remaining letters may be rearranged
aspiration is the breathy h sound, so losing it drops an H

explanation.surface: Going beyond cleverness without perhaps losing ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing aspiration' drops H from WITHOUT to leave WITOUT, which 'possibly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwit someone is to beat them by being cleverer.

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the letters of hears are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone learns about an ancient people.
explanation.definitionFit: Asher was one of the twelve tribes of Israel.

clue.text: Remained sober by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says a word is heard rather than read

parts.note: staid means sober and sedate

explanation.surface: Stayed teetotal, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: Stayed means stopped on in one place, the same as remained.

parts.note: not oversleeping: raise the late, meaning the dead, from the ground

explanation.surface: An order to have a lie-in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' means deceased, and 'get up' means dig up.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhume is to dig a buried body out of the grave.

clue.text: Sweet smell of a foreign city

parts.note: Roma is the Italian name for Rome, a foreign city

explanation.surface: The fragrance of some city abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a pleasant scent.

clue.text: A politician, one making a plea

parts.note: Lib is short for a Liberal politician
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A politician pleads his case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a defence claiming the accused was elsewhere, used as an excuse.

parts.note: a small stroke projecting beyond the main stroke of a printed letter

explanation.surface: Goes past the mark.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'line' is the stroke of a letter in typography, not a finishing line.
explanation.definitionFit: A serif is the small cross-stroke at the end of a letter's main stroke in certain typefaces.

clue.text: One is in revolt, spending year in the country

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'One is in revolt, spending year in the country'. SYRIA has Y inside SRIA, but no reading of 'One is in revolt' gives SRIA; the wordplay cannot be recovered.
annotationWithheld.clue: One is in revolt, spending year in the country

parts.note: relatively read as among relatives: a nasty argument between kin

explanation.surface: A fairly nasty argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relatively' seems to mean 'fairly'; it means 'among relatives'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispute between relations, such as siblings or cousins, is so called.

clue.text: One in the centre of business perhaps

definitions.text: One in the centre of business perhaps

parts.words: One in the centre of business perhaps
parts.note: a person who sits literally in the middle, between producer and buyer

explanation.surface: Someone at the heart of commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: A middleman is an intermediary trader between producer and consumer.
